 The first in a series of storms expected to reach San Diego County late Thursday 
 Forecasters are unsure how much rain the systems will bring to the region

 A wave crashes over the break wall at the Children’s Pool in La Jolla during a high tide Tuesday in San Diego. (K.C. Alfred / The San Diego Union-Tribune)
 By Gary Robbins PUBLISHED: November 11, 2026 at 1:52 PM PST | UPDATED: November 12, 2026 at 5:22 PM PST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... The first of what may be three consecutive storms will move ashore before dawn Friday in San Diego County, delivering light precipitation that could be followed by heavy rain on Monday, the National Weather Service says.
 Forecasters believe a piece of the huge storm that’s expected to hit Northern and Central California on Friday and Saturday will drop south and curl into Baja California. Some of that moisture will likely spread into greater San Diego.
 “We’re kind of fuzzy on this because we don’t exactly know where the moisture will go,” said Miguel Miller, a weather service forecaster. “We might get 0.4 inches or more of rain.”
 He said that a much stronger system could target Southern California on Monday and generate strong waves that could cause more erosion along the coast. Weather models suggest that a third storm would follow on Wednesday.
 San Diego won’t be getting the huge, El Niño-enhanced high tides during these storms. But the weather service is concerned about potentially record tides during the Thanksgiving holiday.
